videos.script: Lesson 32 returned errors and passed them up exactly as they came. This lesson makes them say more. {{new}} First, errors.New itself. Two errors made from the same words are not the same error, and its source shows why. {{errorf}} Then fmt.Errorf, which builds an error the way Printf builds a line. Its most important job is adding context. Each function on the way up writes what it was doing, and the message reads left to right, from the outermost step to the cause. {{verbs}} Two verbs add those words. Percent v copies the old error's text. Percent w copies the text and keeps the old error inside the new one. The output looks the same, and it is not the same. {{style}} You will also see what a message looks like when every layer writes a capital letter and a full stop. {{several}} Last, one error made from several, with errors.Join, and what you promise a caller when you wrap. By the end, an error from your program tells a person what failed and where.
